notes: Matching was by overlapping anchor position in the source text. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance on disclosure duties (A 'require', B 'permit'); resolved to permit because the codebook reserves require for AI use itself being required. (2) Type choices where the two coders read a sentence at different levels: P09 vs P04 vs P66 for instructor statement duties (resolved by whether the sentence tells instructors to state/write the rule, P09, or to discuss it, P66), P29 vs P06, P19 vs P32, P36 vs P28, P63 vs P09 for sample syllabus language, P22 vs P09 vs P66 for the smart-glasses communication sentence; assessment-reversal sentence moved to UNCOVERED. (3) Modality followed the source wording (should-not vs must-not, should vs must). (4) Phase for resource offers resolved to general; for syllabus drafting advice to before-course. (5) Actor: descriptive sentences to all, instructor-addressed duties to instructor. A found many more units than B overall, mostly in the Teaching With AI page (99 vs 52): 58 A-only units were kept after checking the source (separate bullets and sentences coded as one unit by B), 10 A-only units were dropped as rationale clauses, link lists, navigation or non-AI wording; all 5 B-only units were kept (CLAS sanction tiers, reporting rule, written-and-oral information, goals-and-values sentence). Document stance (delegates) agreed in all 5 documents.
